title: I Gave Stockfish 1 Snake Until I LOSE
summary: Reverse-odds series: Fairy-Stockfish (level 8, lichess-style UI) gets only its king plus N Snakes (start 1, +1 after each narrator win) vs the narrator's army. Snake = moves like a bishop but captures like a knight. Narrator wins with 1-6 snakes mostly by pushing rook-supported passed pawns and ladder mates; loses one game against 7 snakes and then draws a 7-snake rematch by the 50-move rule; against 8 snakes he hangs his queen and concedes.
rules: Snake (fairy piece): non-capturing moves slide like a bishop; captures only like a knight (L-jump). It cannot capture along diagonals, so a pawn can 'boot' it safely.
Engine side: king + N snakes (N = 1 in game 1, +1 per game). No other engine pieces/pawns (frames show king plus a back rank of snakes).

Narrator side: standard pawns, rooks, queen and king; the fairy pieces that the variant normally places on the back rank (minor-piece squares) were removed ('removed the extra fairy pieces from our first rank').
Normal chess rules otherwise: castling, promotion, 50-move rule, stalemate = draw.
win_condition: Checkmate Fairy-Stockfish; each win adds one snake for the next game; the run ends when the player loses (concedes vs 8 snakes in the video).
